, expanding access to advanced chip-design technology as competition intensifies over the cost and performance of AI computing. The partnership could strengthen Amazon Web Services' ability to develop specialized processors while giving Synopsys a significant commercial opportunity in custom silicon.

Synopsys is a leading provider of electronic design automation software and semiconductor intellectual property, helping chipmakers design, test and validate increasingly complex processors. Its technology is used throughout the semiconductor industry, making custom-chip development an important growth opportunity.

Announced Wednesday, the agreement expands a relationship spanning more than 15 years and will provide Amazon with Synopsys' application-specific chip technology, design software and simulation tools.
The arrangement supports AWS's growing portfolio of internally developed processors, including Graviton and Trainium, alongside chips supporting networking, storage and cloud security.
The companies will also collaborate on integrating artificial intelligence into semiconductor design and system testing.
The partnership runs both ways: Synopsys plans to use AWS infrastructure to develop its own chip-design products, including Amazon Bedrock to build new AI-powered engineering tools.

"Special purpose silicon is at the heart of AWS innovation. As we expand into application-optimized IP solutions, we're proud to have Amazon as our lead customer for this next phase of growth, Synopsys CEO Sassine Ghazi said.

title: Amazon Makes $1 Billion Bet on Next-Generation Chips
